quote: October is the only month I leave the house dressed for a blizzard and come home carrying half my outfit.
caption: The coat came off at the mailbox. The scarf at the second tree. By the front door I was carrying a small wardrobe and a mild grudge against the weather forecast. It was 41 degrees when I left. It's 68 now. I stood on the porch with my hat in one hand and a glove on the floor, doing the math on whether to go back for it. I did not go back for it. The glove can walk home on its own.
first: I keep a spare pair of gloves in the car now, just so I can lose them in shifts. My husband says there are four mismatched ones in the glovebox. I told him they're a collection.
alt: Cartoon illustration of a flushed, wry woman coming up a sunny porch strewn with orange leaves, arms overflowing with a puffy coat, chunky scarf, knit hat and gloves, one glove dropping. Text at the top reads: October is the only month I leave the house dressed for a blizzard and come home carrying half my outfit.
